subject: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@orka.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps

Hi Alice —

Quick update from our side: between 03:45–04:10 PT this morning one of the reserved GPU pools assigned to your dedicated capacity experienced an eviction spike caused by a transient node failure combined with an aggressive autoscaling step. This led to ~12% of your requests either being queued or routed to fallback instances for ~11 minutes.

What we did: 
- Automated fallback to compatible hosted variants was triggered to keep request flow alive (you may have seen slightly higher latency and model variant metadata).
- We throttled autoscaler aggressiveness for the pool to prevent repeated re-evictions.
- Collected eviction logs and request traces (attached).

Impact observed for Orka Systems: 
- Brief elevation in tail latency for streaming calls (~200–350ms extra)
- ~0.6% of tokens served by fallback model variant (compatibility-checked)

Immediate next steps we’re taking: 
1) Full post-incident analysis and a remediation runbook (ETA EOD PT)
2) A proposal for a short-term throttling policy and a canary window to validate stability (we recommend a 72-hour canary)
3) SLA credit calculation based on your committed reserved capacity (we’ll share the calc)

I’m assigning Marissa (ops lead) and Monica (technical account lead) to coordinate remediation and credits. I’ll follow up with a concrete timeline in the next 2 hours.

I’m very sorry for the disruption — I know you rely on predictable throughput. Please tell me if you want us to pause fallback and fail instead (not recommended) while we repair nodes.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: eviction_logs_20270422.zip (log bundle, 18MB), fallback-policy-v1.pdf (2 pages)

From: Alice Wong <alice@orka.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orka.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps

Thanks for the quick note, Karthik.

We saw elevated latency on several production endpoints and one customer reported dropped responses during the window. The product team is concerned about correctness risk when fallback model variants are used — they want to understand the variant mapping and whether any prompts might have returned subtly different formatting.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Please share which model variant(s) were used as fallback and the mapping rules for compatibility checks.
2) We will need the SLA credit calc and an expected remediation ETA for the dedicated pool.

I’ve looped in procurement because we may need to formalize credits against the reserved capacity contract.

Alice Wong
Head of Platform Engineering, Orka Systems
alice@orka.com

> Quick update from our side: between 03:45–04:10 PT this morning one of the reserved GPU pools assigned to your dedicated capacity experienced an eviction spike...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@orka.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps

Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: 
- Fallback variants: we routed to model family rdx-large-compat-v2 (same tokenizer; output formatting preserved by a validation layer). We attached the variant mapping table and compatibility rules in fallback-policy-v1.pdf.
- SLA credit calc: we ran the numbers and have a preliminary Excel attached (SLA_credit_calc_ORKA.xlsx).
- Remediation ETA: MARISSA will lead the pool remediation; initial safe window begins at 18:00 PT tonight with a 72-hour canary. Final fix (kernel patch + autoscaler tuning) is targeted within 5 business days.

Action items for Orka (recommended, quick): 
- Share any prompt examples where you observed different formatting so we can validate content-level regressions.
- Approve the 72-hour canary window so we can test throttling policy.

Marissa and Monica — I’m handing this to you to coordinate the technical work and the credit. Sean, please advise on the proposed customer comms and credit wording.

Thanks all,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps

Adding the remediation plan and immediate ops notes: 

Summary of root cause (prelim): transient host power-cycle during an aggressive scale-out event + a race in our eviction reconciliation logic that retriggered additional evictions. That produced short-lived resource pressure and forced some sessions onto fallback nodes.

Remediation steps (timeline):
- 11:30–12:30 PT: soft-tuning applied (reduction of scale-out aggressiveness; hold window expanded) — completed.
- 18:00 PT tonight: controlled canary with throttling policy applied to Orka pool (duration 72h). We will route a fraction of traffic to dedicated pool with tighter preemption thresholds.
- 5 business days: kernel-level patch + reconciliation fix to eviction controller; post-deploy soak and validation.

Attachments: SLA_credit_calc_ORKA.xlsx — I’ve populated the credit calc with token counts and estimated impacted minutes.

Customer comms draft (for Sean): 
"We experienced a short-lived capacity disruption affecting a portion of your dedicated pool on 2027-04-22. Automated fallback kept traffic online, but you may have observed higher latencies and small formatting differences on a limited set of responses. We will apply a 72-hour canary starting 18:00 PT to validate fixes and will issue a credit for impacted reserved capacity. Detailed logs and our remediation timeline are attached."

Sean — can you please tighten the wording for external consumption and confirm the credit language? Karthik — please send to Alice once reviewed.

-Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@orka.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool eviction spike — automated fallback activated & next steps

Alice —

Thanks for flagging this and for your patience. We’re sorry for the disruption. Below is the formal comms and the credit offer we propose; we will follow up with a formal DocuSign amendment if procurement requests it.

External comms (final):
Hi Alice / Orka team,

We experienced a short-lived capacity disruption on 2027-04-22 that affected a subset of your reserved GPU pool. To preserve availability we engaged an automated fallback to compatible hosted model variants; this may have caused brief increases in latency and a very small number of responses with format differences.

What we’re doing: 
- Active remediation of the pool; we have a 72-hour canary starting 18:00 PT tonight.
- A kernel patch and controller fix targeted for 5 business days.
- Issuing a pro-rated SLA credit for the impacted minutes on your reserved capacity (see attached calc).

If you prefer, we can pause fallback behavior and fail fast while we repair (not recommended for production traffic). Please confirm whether you’d like us to proceed with the canary as scheduled.

Credit offer summary: pro-rated credit equal to impacted reserved-node minutes multiplied by your committed monthly rate (details in SLA_credit_calc_ORKA.xlsx). We will not bill for the impacted minutes and will reflect the credit on the next invoice.

Please reply to confirm the canary window.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Attachments: SLA_credit_calc_ORKA.xlsx

Sean / Karthik —

Thanks for the level of detail and the proposed remediation. We accept the 72-hour canary beginning tonight and appreciate the credit proposal. Procurement will coordinate the DocuSign amendment if needed.

We did capture two example prompts that returned slightly different formatting during the window — I’ve attached them to this thread in a follow-up email to Monica for validation. Please loop back with confirmation once the canary is live.

Alice
